label: PF Backlog 632
title: Process: Gate 1 must embed the latest Gate 1.5 evidence + a design pre-check checklist to reduce review churn

brief.problem: Gate 1.5 review evidence is easy to skip at Gate 1; the same blocker/major finding classes recur every review with no learning loop.
brief.what_adds: A Gate 1 pending-blocking check, a design pre-check checklist, direct-call 1.5/2.5 defaults, and a findings->correction-ledger learning loop with a durable trend report.
brief.why: Makes reviews pre-empt recurring findings instead of re-discovering them; keeps Gate 1 decisions evidence-based.
brief.who_feels: HIL approvers, item authors, and reviewers.

objective: Make Gate 1.5 evidence binding at Gate 1 and cut review churn by pre-empting recurring findings: a design pre-check checklist, a Gate 1 pending-blocking check, direct-call 1.5/2.5 defaults, and a findings->correction-ledger learning loop.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic check (scripts/dev/gate1_check.py --item <ID>) renders the consolidated Gate 1.5 findings+dispositions and exits non-zero when any BLOCKER or MAJOR is still PENDING.

Gate 1 requires BOTH the consolidated view (architect_review.py gate --item <ID> --gate 1) and the enforcement check (gate1_check.py); both are documented as binding in docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md.

A design pre-check checklist covering recurring blocker classes is emitted before Gate 1.5: it is auto-included in every design-mode review prompt (architect_review.py run --mode design) and available via checklist --item <ID>.
Gate 1.5/2.5 default to the direct provider call (architect_review.py run); the sub-agent launch is opt-in only and both paths are documented in config/architect-review.json and docs.

Recurring findings are captured as CORRECTION-LEDGER entries each with an enforcement point, and the findings-per-review trend is persisted to the registered engineering/learnings/review-findings.json report consumed by RAG-PROCESS-MEMORY.
A test covers the PENDING-blocking behaviour: the Gate 1 check fails when a BLOCKER/MAJOR is undispensed and passes when all findings are dispositioned.
approach: Process: Gate 1 must embed the latest Gate 1.5 evidence + a design pre-check checklist to reduce review churn
verification: precheck fast PASS (45 gates) on the branch; Gate 2.5 architect review clean (0 findings) for the final diff.
risks: new check could be noisy if severity is miscalibrated
trend report needs RAG retrieval wired separately
rollback: revert the tooling/doc change; the consolidated renderer already exists.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/merge_gate.py (or a new gate validator) and core/code_quality_gate.py so the Gate 1 validation reads the latest Gate 1.5 evidence (via /api/v1/evidence/index + manifest) and enforces a design pre-check checklist loaded from config/ci-cd-gates.json. Add a small checklist schema + validation; reuse evidence event APIs and design_critic.py signals for pre-check scoring.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES Gate 1.5 evidence pipeline producing /api/v1/evidence/events data
RELATED BI-0205 (PR pre-check gates) — same checklist source of truth
conflict_findings: BI-0205 touches config/ci-cd-gates.json and gate modules — coordinate checklist config edits
No other concurrent items modify merge_gate.py per backlog data
duplication_findings: BI-0205 defines pre-check gates in the PR workflow — align checklist with its existing pre-check stages
BI-0443 introduces a dependency/manifest-diff pre-check hook — checklist should include its rule
No existing item gates on Gate 1.5 evidence embedding — no true duplicate
analysis.rationale: Existing gate modules and evidence APIs cover ~80% of the need; this is an EXTEND of merge_gate/code_quality_gate with a config-driven checklist, not new capability.
assumptions: Gate 1.5 evidence is already emitted via /api/v1/evidence/events
config/ci-cd-gates.json is the canonical place for gate checklists
Gate 1 is enforced server-side in merge_gate.py or code_quality_gate.py
risks: Gate 1.5 evidence may be missing or stale for some items — need fallback behavior
Checklist too rigid → recreates churn it aims to reduce
Overlap with BI-0205 pre-check gates could double-gate same signals
evidence: core/merge_gate.py + core/code_quality_gate.py exist as gate enforcement points
missing_info: Exact definition/schema of the Gate 1.5 evidence artifact
Concrete items in the design pre-check checklist (who authors them?)
Behavior when Gate 1.5 evidence is absent: block vs warn
Whether BI-0205 has already implemented overlapping pre-checks

context_review.reason: Every field is a verbatim copy of the title; no specifics on which Gate 1 artifact/template files to edit, what the Gate 1.5 evidence looks like, what checklist items to add, or how success is verified.

api_impact.reason: process/tooling change: no external API surface; adds deterministic dev scripts + docs.
